title: Chris Gotterup claims third PGA Tour win of season after Ben Kohles hits into water on 18
content:
Golf is a game that carries more potential pain lingering in each and every swing than most sports combined. Sunday, Ben Kohles reminded us how thin that line is between glory and agony.

Kohles, tied for the lead and hitting from the 18th fairway with a chance to win the John Deere Classic, sprayed his ball left and into the water at TPC Deere Run to hand the tournament to 26-year-old Chris Gotterup. The double bogey marked the second time Kohles gave away a tournament on the 18th hole in three years.

But Sunday was for Gotterup, a rising star who now has three PGA Tour wins this season and four in the past 12 months.

Gotterup shot a no-bogey Sunday 62 to skyrocket up the leaderboard. Per The Athletic contributor Justin Ray, all three of his 2026 wins have come with a final round 64 or lower — a highlight of one of the more exciting young birdie machines in golf.

For three days in the Quad Cities, Gotterup struggled to find greens. He ranked in the bottom half of the field in approach and entered the final round five shots and six groups behind the leaders.

Sunday, he couldn’t miss, going out on the front nine in 30 and gaining 2.52 strokes on the field in approach as he came out of nowhere to take the clubhouse lead.

Still, it seemed as if the tournament was Kohles’ to lose until he bogeyed 15 and birdied 16 to get back into a tie with Gotterup. The energy may have shifted when he failed to birdie the par-5 17th. The missed opportunity should still have sent him to a playoff, or, better yet, to a victory if he could birdie 18. He’s played most of the season on the Korn Ferry Tour, and this win would have cemented his PGA Tour status going forward.

Instead, that ball ended up in the water, and his chances were gone.

It was just two years ago that Kohles was a flubbed chip away from changing his career forever. He held a one-shot lead standing near the green on the 18th hole of the CJ Cup Byron Nelson. Instead, his chip failed to reach the green, and he bogeyed while Taylor Pendrith snagged the tourney from Kohles’ grasp.

As for Gotterup, the win cements 12 months of ascendance. A little less than a year ago, Gotterup held off Rory McIlroy to win the Scottish Open. He then contended at the Open Championship and made a case for a Ryder Cup spot despite not being selected.

This season, he’s proven he should have been picked. He’s won the Sony Open, the Waste Management Phoenix Open and now the John Deere to tally five career wins. It’s safe to say he’ll be on the Presidents Cup team this fall.
